content.thinking: I need to fix that phrasing to something clearer, like "during every evaluation logged, it was on."

action_items.item: Make CI run the account-page tests with each rollout flag switched on, including an account with past purchases but none this month, so that a change to code behind a flag is tested on the path the flag selects.
Find out how revision 383534e came to be deployed to production when Code-Fix found it not in main's history, and whether it passed review.
Ramp io-shop feature flags up in steps, checking the error rate between steps, instead of switching them on for most traffic at once.
Do not switch on a flag in the same minute as a deploy that changes the code it gates: wait until the deploy is seen healthy with the flag off.
Once the fix is merged, deploy a revision carrying it to io-shop in place of revision 383534e. The recorded_at change in 383534e is not in main, so its owner must decide whether it ships.

Before monthly-spend-feature is switched back on, have the statement panel's owner decide whether render_monthly_statement should still raise for an empty month. Code-Fix read it as raising ValueError there and found the flag named as gating that panel.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is brought in.
Find out why the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, and restore it so that rollbacks of io-shop can be done.

causal_chain.step: Some shoppers' account page requests failed. Account-page error warnings rose above their usual level, and the error rate the alert watches (the share of all the service's requests answered with a server error) stayed above its threshold until the alert fired.

Those requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The account page's request boundary catches any exception and returns a failed page, so the whole page failed and not just one figure.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee at {P1.1}: the metrics read across the hours before the onset show the service at its usual error rate with that revision in place. Account pages were logged rendering normally, and the flag was logged off, up to the onset.

Revision 383534e, deployed at {P2.1}, breaking pages without the flag: after the flag was switched off, the service left the incident's level and the revert was confirmed. The rollback of that revision was never done, so it was still running when the service recovered.

causal_chain.step: Requests reached the monthly spend average in spend_summary.py because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P3.1}. At {G971b.6} most of the flag's evaluations came back on, and during {Gce95.4} every evaluation logged was on. When a request's monthly-summary rollout decision is on, render_spend_summary sends it to average_spend_per_item_this_month.

The monthly average failed for shoppers with no purchase recorded this month because revision 383534e had removed its empty-month guard. That revision was deployed at {P2.1}, and at {T10.1} it was running on every replica.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change removed the step that handled shoppers who had bought nothing this month, and when a new feature that uses that code was switched on, the account page failed for those shoppers.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that caught the removal of the empty-month guard before revision 383534e was deployed. By Code-Fix's reading of the test file, no existing test ran the monthly path for an account with past purchases but none this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test running the monthly path for a shopper with no purchases this month would have failed on that revision, and it would not have reached production in that form.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag was switched on for most traffic at once, at the same instant as the deploy that changed the code it gates, with no gradual ramp seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Exposing the new code to a small slice first would have limited the failures to that slice and shown the error rise before most shoppers were reached.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

got_lucky: The faulty code was reached only through a flag, which Argus could switch off through the flag provider while the deployment platform was unreachable. The pages recovered without a rollback.

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the diff of the deploy that landed at the onset, which shows the empty-month guard removed.
Argus moved on to the flag candidate C2 when the rollback for C1 could not be done.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off. The action can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent watched the service leave the incident's level and judged the revert confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so no person was brought in, even when the rollback could not be done.
The rollback of revision 383534e could not be done because the deployment platform's API answered {T19.2}, so the revision without the guard was left running.

input.root_cause: Revision 383534e removed from average_spend_per_item_this_month the guard that returned {D1.1} for a shopper who had bought nothing this month, and changed it to count only purchases whose recorded_at falls in the current month. For any shopper with no such purchase, it now floor-divides total_this_month_cents by the length of an empty list and raises ZeroDivisionError. The account page's request boundary catches that error and fails the whole page.
input.still_at_risk: While revision 383534e stays running, switching monthly-spend-feature back on would fail account pages again for shoppers with no purchase recorded this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
